name: whatsapp-api
description: WhatsApp service built on Baileys: SQLite store, media pipeline, REST surface
//files: What `pnpm deploy --prod` copies into a runtime image. Without it the deploy carries `src/` - every `*.test.ts`, both test-scaffolding modules and the fixtures - into a published container. The SDK already declares the same thing for the same reason.
//scripts: Every script that reads `whatsapp-api-sdk` — at type level or at runtime — builds it first via `build:deps`, so a bare `pnpm --filter whatsapp-api <script>` cannot outrun the SDK build the way it would if only the root scripts sequenced it. `^...` is pnpm for "this package's workspace dependencies, excluding itself", so the list does not have to be maintained by hand. The SDK's own build is `tsc -b`, which is up-to-date-aware: when `dist/` is already current the nested call writes nothing, so the root's parallel `pnpm -r` fan-out cannot have two compilers emitting into `packages/sdk/dist` at once. `start` is deliberately not in the list: it runs the built artifact and presupposes a build.
